lead: Battery current and voltage sensing measure the electrical flow into and out of a battery pack. They let the battery management system (BMS) estimate state of charge (SOC), state of health (SOH) and state of function (SOF). Electric vehicles, hybrid cars and stop-start systems use these estimates to protect cells, report range and control charging. Only a few universities teach this chapter. A shunt resistor or Hall sensor measures current; a resistor divider feeding an isolated amplifier measures voltage; software combines both with temperature.

sections.h3: Current sensing with shunt and Hall sensors

blocks.text: Current is the rate of charge flow. One ampere is one coulomb per second. A battery pack can carry hundreds of amperes. A shunt resistor is a low-value resistor placed in series with the pack. The shunt voltage is V<sub>shunt</sub> = I × R<sub>shunt</sub>, where V<sub>shunt</sub> is the voltage in volts, I is the current in amperes and R<sub>shunt</sub> is the shunt resistance in ohms. A 0.1 mΩ shunt at 100 A gives 10 mV. The amplifier raises this small signal before the ADC. A Kelvin connection uses separate force and sense terminals so lead resistance does not add to the measured voltage. Shunt resistance changes with temperature, so the BMS compensates using a temperature sensor. A Hall current sensor measures the magnetic field produced by the current. It gives isolation and no insertion loss, which suits high-voltage packs. Its offset and low-current accuracy are weaker. The BMS must also record current direction: discharge is one sign, regenerative braking current is the opposite sign.

Each cell or module needs a voltage reading. A resistor divider scales a pack voltage down to the ADC range: Vadc = Vpack × R2 / (R1 + R2), where Vadc is the ADC input voltage, Vpack is the pack voltage and R1, R2 are the divider resistors. The divider must have high resistance to avoid draining the pack, but high resistance makes it sensitive to ADC input current. An isolated amplifier or isolated ADC keeps the low-voltage electronics safe from the high-voltage pack. For an n-bit ADC with reference Vref, one count is Vref / (2n − 1), the same rule as in the other sensor chapters. A 12-bit ADC with a 5 V reference has a step of 5 ÷ 4095 = 1.22 mV. Battery modules often carry a small cell-voltage monitor that sends readings to the BMS. Temperature sensing uses thermistors, as in throttle position and temperature sensors. The BMS combines cell voltage, pack current and temperature before it estimates SOC, SOH and SOF.

sections.h3: SOC, SOH, SOF and coulomb counting

blocks.text: State of charge (SOC) is the remaining charge as a fraction of rated capacity. State of health (SOH) describes ageing, usually capacity fade and resistance rise. State of function (SOF) is the power the pack can deliver or accept now; it depends on SOC, temperature and SOH, because an aged cell has a higher resistance. Coulomb counting integrates current: SOC(t) = SOC(0) − (1/C<sub>n</sub>) ∫ I dt, where SOC(t) is the present fraction, SOC(0) is the starting fraction, C<sub>n</sub> is the rated capacity in ampere-hours, I is current in amperes with discharge positive, and t is time in hours. In discrete form, ΔSOC = −I × Δt / C<sub>n</sub>, so a discharge (I positive) lowers SOC. The estimate drifts because a small current offset or gain error is integrated hour after hour; a stale C<sub>n</sub> after capacity fade is a scale error on top of that. The BMS resets it with open-circuit voltage (OCV) after the pack has rested, when cell voltage reflects SOC. OCV is flat in the middle SOC range, so the reset is strongest near empty or full. Current, voltage and thermal sensing together support SOC, SOH and SOF.

examples.question: A 50 Ah battery starts at SOC 80%. It discharges at 10 A for 30 min. Find the charge removed and the new SOC by coulomb counting.
steps: Charge removed ΔQ = I × Δt = 10 A × 0.5 h = 5 Ah.
SOC drop = ΔQ / C<sub>n</sub> = 5 Ah / 50 Ah = 0.10 = 10%.
examples.answer: 5 Ah is removed and the new SOC is 70%.
examples.check:
I = 10.0
dt_h = 30 / 60
capacity = 50.0
soc0 = 80.0
dq = I * dt_h
drop = dq / capacity * 100
soc = soc0 - drop
print(f'{dq:g}')
print(f'{drop:g}')
print(f'{soc:g}')

traps: Coulomb counting drifts because a current offset is integrated; a stale capacity value adds a scale error. Reset with OCV after rest and relearn C<sub>n</sub>.
A shunt needs a Kelvin connection and temperature compensation, or lead and shunt resistance errors enter the reading.
Regenerative braking reverses current direction; a wrong sign makes SOC rise during discharge.
SOC, SOH and SOF are different: SOC is charge now, SOH is ageing, SOF is power capability.

quiz.a: SOC is remaining charge as a fraction of rated capacity; SOH is ageing, mainly capacity fade and resistance rise.

quiz.q: Why can a Hall current sensor suit a high-voltage pack?
quiz.a: It measures current magnetically, so it gives isolation and no shunt insertion loss; offset and low-current accuracy are weaker.

quiz.q: A 60 Ah battery at SOC 50% discharges at 6 A for 1 h. Find the new SOC by coulomb counting.
quiz.a: Charge removed = 6 × 1 = 6 Ah. SOC drop = 6/60 = 10%. New SOC = 50 − 10 = 40%.

quiz.q: A coulomb counter shows 0 A at rest after its offset was zeroed, yet its SOC disagrees with the OCV check by 8 % after a week of driving. Give two causes and one reset method.
quiz.a: A gain error in the current sensor (it reads, say, 2 % high under load, which is integrated over every trip) and a stale rated capacity C<sub>n</sub> after the cells have faded. Reset: rest the pack, read OCV, set SOC from the OCV curve, and relearn C<sub>n</sub> from two such resets.

quiz.q: What does a Kelvin connection do in a shunt?
quiz.a: Separate force and sense terminals stop lead resistance from adding to the shunt voltage.

quiz.q: Why is OCV reset unreliable in the middle SOC range?
quiz.a: The OCV–SOC curve is flat there, so a small voltage error gives a large SOC error.

quiz.q: What does state of function (SOF) mean?
quiz.a: The power the pack can deliver or accept right now; it depends on SOC, temperature and SOH (internal resistance).

beyond: Not for the exam. Production BMSs combine coulomb counting with Kalman filters and electrochemical models. Cell balancing and thermal management use the same voltage and temperature sensors. Search for battery management system SOC estimation, shunt-based current sensing and isolated cell voltage monitoring.
